item.title: WA group, engineers & race against time: How 2 workers were rescued from Nepal tunnel
item.description: In a remarkable display of resilience, two workers were saved from a collapsed tunnel after being trapped for nine long days. Rescuers encountered significant obstacles while clearing the thick mud, necessitating advanced equipment and expertise. An engineers' WhatsApp group played an essential role by exchanging real-time updates, ultimately leading to this unexpected yet joyous rescue effort that rekindled hope amid adversity.

item.title: Alberta Premier Danielle Smith’s message to international students: Study, then return home
item.description: Alberta's Premier Danielle Smith has made it clear that international students need to leave Canada once their study visas expire. She highlighted that these visas serve as temporary permits meant for academic pursuits, urging students to return to their home countries. This statement follows rising concerns over immigration programs misleading students about potential residency outcomes. With Canada tightening its immigration policies, unauthorized work could lead to serious repercussions.

item.title: Detroit Zoo helps send 500 rare snails back to Tahiti after 37-year effort
item.description: Hundreds of tiny snails are journeying over 5,000 miles from Michigan to Tahiti. This release is part of a long-running international conservation program for endangered native snails. Invasive predators had caused severe population collapses for these unique mollusks in their native islands. The Detroit Zoo has been breeding and caring for these snails since 1989. This ongoing effort has successfully returned over 17,000 snails to their natural habitat.

item.title: Travis Kelce’s $1.5m nonprofit under scrutiny: Why did charity spending raise questions?
item.description: Travis Kelce’s Eighty-Seven and Running Foundation is facing scrutiny over its reported spending between 2021 and 2024. The nonprofit raised $1.5 million and spent about $1.1 million, with $469,000 listed for management and $446,000 for charity. Kelce’s business manager Aaron Eanes disputed the figures, saying some charitable operational costs were misclassified. He said management fees dropped to zero in 2025 as the foundation works to improve transparency and governance.

item.title: Why IIT and IIM students are ditching backpacks for buckets and bicycles
item.description: The “No-Bag Day” trend is gaining popularity on Indian higher-education campuses, with students at IIT Bombay and IIM Lucknow replacing conventional backpacks with buckets, umbrellas, cardboard boxes, chairs and even bicycles. The student-led activity offers a playful break from demanding academic routines while encouraging creativity and camaraderie. Inspired by the international “Anything But a Bag Day” concept, the trend has also appeared at other Indian colleges, turning an ordinary campus day into a memorable experience.

Flash floods triggered by an ice-rock avalanche devastated towns and villages.

item.title: Game on, history off: White House unveils MAGA arcade
item.description: The White House launched retro-style video games to promote President Trump's agenda. Two immigration games, 'Build the Wall' and 'Rio Run,' sparked significant controversy. Critics argue these games trivialize serious immigration issues and dehumanize migrants. Supporters believe the administration is communicating policy in an accessible language for younger Americans. This initiative reflects a broader effort to reshape America's historical narrative.

item.title: Pak coach Hesson breaks silence on shake-up, says 'I don't know what happened'
item.description: Mike Hesson, the interim coach for Pakistan, has refuted any claims of his involvement in the decision to send home senior players. He clarified that Mohammad Rizwan, Salman Ali Agha, and Imam-ul-Haq had already departed. Hesson is now focused on fine-tuning the squad for the final Test, emphasizing a well-rounded bowling lineup with greater diversity, while integrating new talent to enhance team balance.
